questions.prompt: You 3-bet preflop and the flop is A72 rainbow. You have AQ. Best default?

choices.text: Bet. Top pair is strong in a 3-bet pot and the board is dry.
Min-bet and fold to a tiny raise
Treat it like a limped pot and check the nuts-adjacent hand

questions.explanation: This is value and a range advantage. Bet.

questions.prompt: You called a 3-bet in position with 76s and missed a dry ace-high flop. Best default?

choices.text: Fold to a bet, or check back if they check. You have almost no equity.

questions.explanation: Suited connectors need a flop. This one missed. 3-bet pots do not pay floats the way single-raised pots do.

questions.prompt: You have KK in a 3-bet pot on 9h 8h 7c. Best default?

choices.text: Bet, but respect a large raise. The board is wet and your overpair is no longer the nuts.

questions.explanation: An overpair bets for value and protection. A shove or a big raise can mean a straight or a set.

questions.prompt: Stack-to-pot ratio is about 4. You have top pair top kicker on a dry board. Getting it in…

choices.text: Is often correct. There is not enough room to fold later.

questions.explanation: Low SPR means one pair of good quality is a commit hand on safe boards.
